ravi: Quick heads-up — astera21b mixed-int6 canary is OOMing in perf smoke when batch_size >= 4. Repro on canary-03 and canary-04.

joanna: logs? which step is blowing up?

ravi: stack trace + memlog below. looks like KV cache growth + slab fragmentation. reproducer: send 4 concurrent gen requests (~max_new_tokens=512) with long context.

ravi: ```
[2026-03-22T19:11:02Z] OOM: allocation failed: 112MiB
node: canary-03
pid: 8142
model: astera21b-mixed-int6
stage: forward_kernel (attention_kv)
heap_frag: 0.62
active_slots: 3
batch_size: 4
max_new_tokens: 512
stack: kernel_alloc+0x1a3
```

eli: hm. mixed-int6 group-quant often increases temporary buffer peaks during KV concat. Did we enable per-request prefetch?

ravi: prefetch=true in current canary. I also see repeated small allocations (lots of 4–16KiB).

sasha: try disabling prefetch or reduce prefetch windows first. also try reserve_slots=0.25 on the pool to keep a small cushion.

joanna: on infra side, can we verify allocator free-list merges? last patch to slab-coalesce landed on canary-02 only. canary-03/04 still on older runtime.

infra-bot: deploy status: canary-02 -> runtime v2.14 (slab-coalesce enabled). canary-03/04 -> runtime v2.13 (no coalesce).

eli: ok two-pronged: (1) quick mitigation: lower default max_new_tokens to 256 for astera21b on canary group and set batching.max_batch_size=2 for the next hour; (2) longer: enable slab-coalesce on remaining canaries + test mixed-int6 kernel fallback to int8 for attention_kv.

ravi: I ran the reduced defaults locally — no OOM with batch=2 and max_new_tokens=256. Eval quality looks close on our smoke prompt set (delta ~0.6% perplexity).

sasha: can you paste the smoke eval numbers? want to ensure we don't regress beyond threshold.

ravi: ```
smoke set (50 samples)
- baseline fp16: ppl 18.2
- mixed-int6 (batch2,max256): ppl 18.7 (+2.7%)
- mixed-int6 (batch4,max512): OOM on 12/50 runs
```

joanna: +2.7% is acceptable for initial canary. we can do a quality sweep before promoting.

eli: I'll open a tiny rollout plan: disable prefetch by default, set batching.max_batch_size=2, set default.max_new_tokens=256, and tag canary nodes with runtime v2.14 rollout asap. If quality after full eval is within 3% we'll promote.

sasha: also leaving note to add a microkernel fallback: if attention_kv allocation fails, retry with int8 path (fallback metric). avoids user-facing 500s.

ravi: created repro gist and test script, pushing to /eng-ml/bringups/astera21b/repro.sh and added a quick benchmark.

joanna: action items: eli -> runtime rollout to canary-03/04 (slab-coalesce) by EOD; sasha -> implement fallback retry path; ravi -> run full eval (500 samples) with new defaults and post numbers; I'll coordinate canary routing.

eli: starting rollout now, will report back in thread when v2.14 is on 03/04.

infra-bot: deploy queued: runtime v2.14 -> canary-03. ETA ~8m.

ravi: thanks. leaving note: if anybody sees unusual latency spikes after coalesce, ping me — coalesce changes allocation patterns and might affect tail latency for short queries.

sasha: 👍 will schedule fallback PR today.

eli: deploy complete on canary-03. monitoring for OOM and 95p latency.

infra-bot: deploy complete: canary-03 v2.14. canary-04 pending.

ravi: canary-03 no OOMs in 30m of smoke traffic with batch=3 and max_new_tokens=512 (weirdly stable). leaving thread open until canary-04 done.

joanna: good catch — maybe coalesce gives enough cushion that batch=3 is safe. we'll still keep defaults conservative until full eval.

eli: canary-04 rolled; no new OOMs in 45m. runtime patch seems to have fixed fragmentation. closing for now, follow-up: quality sweep scheduled tomorrow.

sasha: noted follow-up: metric to add -> "allocation_spike_count" per request to detect transient peaks.

ravi: thanks all.
